title: The Fall of Constantinople
description: April-May 1453. The player commands the last defenders of Byzantium under Constantine XI. Hold the Theodosian Walls against Mehmed II's siege: repair breaches from bombard fire, guard the sea walls along the Golden Horn, and survive repeated assaults. Defeat comes if the Hagia Sophia district falls; victory means holding until the final assault is broken.

anachronisms_found: RICHARD_THE_LIONHEART placed as the player's hero: an English king who died in 1199, standing in for Constantine XI Palaiologos (d. 1453) — a 250-year error, and the engine offers Byzantine-flavoured alternatives (e.g. Belisarius, Theodore Lascaris) or at minimum a renamed generic unit

SALADIN placed as the enemy commander: the Ayyubid sultan of the Third Crusade era, used to represent Mehmed II; the dialogue calls him 'Mehmed II' while the placed object is an unambiguously 12th-century Kurdish/Egyptian hero
TREE_PALM_FOREST x20 as the map's only vegetation — palm forest is desert/tropical terrain, wholly wrong for Thrace and the Bosphorus, where pine/oak/Mediterranean tree sets are available

No gunpowder siege whatsoever among placed objects, despite the brief promising 'repair breaches from bombard fire'; the engine has Bombard Cannons and Great Bombards (the Ottoman signature weapon of 1453)
Free-standing GOLD_MINE x11, STONE_MINE x4, FORAGE_BUSH x8 and SHEEP inside/around a besieged imperial capital — random-map economic furniture, not a walled metropolis under blockade

issues_found: Player 1's hero is RICHARD_THE_LIONHEART while the dialogue names Constantine XI — a Third Crusade English king standing in for the last Byzantine emperor, wrong culture and wrong century by 260 years; a renamed generic unit (or Belisarius-style Byzantine placeholder) was available.
Player 2's commander is SALADIN while the text names Mehmed II — an Ayyubid sultan of 1187 substituting for the Ottoman conqueror of 1453; again an unrelated era and dynasty.
Both active players are set to RANDOM civilization, so the Byzantine defenders and Ottoman besiegers may appear with entirely inappropriate architecture and unit rosters.

Defender roster is CROSSBOWMAN and MAN_AT_ARMS only — no hand cannoneers, no bombard cannon or cannon galleons on the Ottoman side, and no Genoese/Venetian contingent; the defining feature of 1453, Orban's great bombards battering the Theodosian Walls, has no representation in placed objects.
TREE_PALM_FOREST x20 gives a desert/tropical vegetation to the Thracian shore of the Bosphorus.

No water, no Golden Horn, no sea walls and no ships at all, despite the brief explicitly requiring the player to guard the sea walls along the Golden Horn; the Ottoman fleet and the chain across the Horn are absent.
No Hagia Sophia district or any distinct inner objective — defeat is keyed to a generic CASTLE and TOWN_CENTER.

Assault waves are described as arriving from north, then east, then south, an invented rotating-wave structure rather than the historical concentration against the Mesoteichion/St Romanus gate and the final pre-dawn assault of 29 May.
Narration asserts 'their attack falters' and the city holds, which inverts the documented outcome; an attentive player would leave believing Constantinople was successfully defended.
Eleven GOLD_MINEs and a full economic build (Market, University, Monastery, Mill, 10 villagers) frame a besieged, starving city as a standard economic base.

Richard the Lionheart is placed as the defenders' hero while the dialogue calls him Constantine XI — a 12th-century English crusader king standing in for the last Byzantine emperor, an avoidable error since any generic unit could have been renamed

Saladin is placed as the besieging commander while the text names Mehmed II — a 12th-century Ayyubid sultan substituting for a 15th-century Ottoman, and the victory condition is keyed to that wrong-era hero
Both players are left as RANDOM civilization, so neither Byzantine nor Turkish architecture, unit rosters, or bonuses are guaranteed; the Theodosian Walls may render in any regional style
TREE_PALM_FOREST x20 gives a tropical/desert vegetation set inappropriate to the Thracian/Marmara littoral

No water at all is placed: the Golden Horn, the sea walls, the Ottoman fleet and the chain across the harbour — all explicitly promised in the brief — are entirely absent, and the 'guard the sea walls' task cannot exist
The Ottoman side has zero gunpowder artillery placed; the brief's central mechanic of repairing breaches from Orban's bombards is reduced to unspecified 'siege weapons' spawned by triggers
No Hagia Sophia district exists; defeat is keyed to a generic Castle and Town Center instead of the landmark the brief names

Defender garrison of 6 Men-at-Arms, 10 Crossbowmen and 10 villagers with a Market, University, Monastery and Stable is a generic town start, not the ~7,000 mixed Greek/Genoese/Venetian garrison; no Genoese contingent (Giustiniani) is represented even by a renamed unit

The narrative asserts a counterfactual outcome — 'their attack falters', 'the final assault is broken' — as the win state, when the historically decisive Kerkoporta/Lycus valley breach and the city's fall are never modelled

A 10-minute hold labelled 'until dawn' compresses a 53-day siege (April 6 – May 29) without acknowledging it, and the assault waves come from north, east and south rather than concentrating on the Mesoteichion
